explanation: Compared against OEIS A241898 (Newman): can every number be written as a sum of four squares none of which is 7²? The statement asserts every n is a² + b² + c² + d² with a, b, c, d ≠ 7. Allowing 0 matches 'at most four squares', as documented. I checked numerically that no n ≤ 20000 fails. Faithful to the OEIS question.
